R178.note: Syntax-tree denylist for arbitrary compiled code is bypassable (e.g. P/Invoke via System.Runtime.InteropServices, or namespace aliasing like `using P = System.Diagnostics;`, is never checked); substring-matched method names ('GetType', 'Invoke', 'CreateInstance') also match unrelated legitimate identifiers, silently rejecting benign rule code that happens to contain those substrings.

R179.note: `--` end-of-options marker correctly passed to tar before operands; matches stated contract exactly, no restriction added.

R180.note: Magic-byte detection plus random filename is the right shape for CWE-434, but the new MIME allowlist (jpeg/png/gif/pdf/text-plain only) is a self-invented restriction that would reject other file types the original denylist implicitly permitted (e.g. docx, zip, csv); disclosed in the write-up but still narrows legitimate uploads.

R181.note: Math.random() replaced with crypto.randomBytes(16), correct API; only observable change is token charset (base64url vs base36), a disclosed, harmless side effect.

R182.note: Removing mark_safe() closes the XSS via Django's default autoescaping, but it also escapes the surrounding trusted `<div class='announcement'>` wrapper the function builds, so the banner now renders as literal tag text instead of formatted HTML - an undisclosed behavior change to the feature's intended output.

R183.note: Standard lock()-then-null-check guard; matches stated contract (skip silently on expired connection, single send on live one).

R184.note: Statement->PreparedStatement with bound parameter; behavior and error handling otherwise unchanged.

R185.note: mongoose.sanitizeFilter() is the framework's own recommended defense for this exact class of NoSQL operator injection; only affects operator-object payloads, legitimate scalar criteria pass through unchanged.

R186.note: realpath()-based canonical containment check plus rejection of scheme/absolute-path/null-byte inputs; removes the chdir() reliance cleanly; no evidence of blocking legitimate report filenames.

R187.note: Bounds check against span.size() instead of an untrusted claimed capacity; dropping the claimedCapacity/advertisedLength parameters is explicitly authorized by the stated contract ('callers no longer need to pass a claimed capacity').

R188.note: unique_ptr->shared_ptr with by-value lambda capture extends the Session's lifetime to cover the queued callback, matching the contract's 'own/share the Session' branch; still enqueues exactly one callback.

R189.note: Null-safe handling in both applyDiscount and the sibling isDiscountApplied, treating missing discount as zero/false exactly per the stated contract.

R190.note: Algorithm pinned to RSA both in keyfunc type assertion and via jwt.WithValidMethods; only rejects non-RS256 tokens, which is the vulnerability itself.

R191.note: SecureRandom replaces attacker-seedable Random; the removed seed parameter had no legitimate purpose (client-controlled token seeding was the vulnerability).

R192.note: secure flag flipped false->true on the existing setcookie() call; no other observable change.

R193.note: Shell elimination via argument-array exec.Command correctly closes the CWE-78 shell-metacharacter vector, but the allowlist regex still permits a leading '-', so a target like '-t' would be passed through as a flag to ping.exe/nslookup.exe (option/flag injection) rather than a hostname literal; no legitimate hostname/IP input is rejected.
